intro: Lumbini, in the plains of southern Nepal, is honoured as the birthplace of the Buddha and draws pilgrims and visitors from across Asia and beyond. On open paved ground by the Mahadevi Temple Road stands a broad Bodhi tree, its grey trunk ringed by a low brick platform and one great limb leaning far out over the paving. A reader sent us its photograph, with visitors walking in its shade, and a note on why such trees matter.

trees.name: The Bodhi Tree of Lumbini

location.address: Mahadevi Temple Road, Lumbini, Rupandehi, Lumbini Province

trees.story:
Lumbini, in the plains of southern Nepal, is honoured as the birthplace of the Buddha, and this broad fig stands on open ground there by the Mahadevi Temple Road, where a reader photographed it with a GPS fix. They wrote: “Lumbini, southern Nepal, is the birthplace of the Buddha. In northern India, to the south, he found enlightenment sitting under a Boddhi tree. There are many such trees at special places associated with the Buddha’s life.”

The photograph shows a tree with room around it. The trunk is a fused mass of grey stems inside a low round brick platform, and two great limbs lean out from it, one reaching far to the right over the paving. The crown is wide and leafy. Visitors in bright clothes walk past and stand in its shade, and a few things lie on a cloth at the foot of the platform.

The reader calls it a Bodhi tree, the sacred fig, Ficus religiosa. We have no age, girth or planting date for it, and we have not found a published record of this particular trunk, so this page states none. If you know its story, tell us here.

Look for the brick platform and the long leaning limb.
